issues.description: coerceNumber silently maps null/non-numeric domain values to 0 instead of propagating NaN/null
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear used toNumber as lift, so non-numeric inputs propagated as NaN downstream. The new coerceNumber returns 0 on null, silently distorting the domain instead of failing loudly. This is a semantic change hidden inside a 'just added types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new contract.

issues.description: Parameter type number[] is weaker than the actual NonEmptyArray precondition enforced at runtime
issues.detail: The pan/zoom signatures advertise number[] but the body asserts non-emptiness via isNonEmpty and throws otherwise. The type system already supports the stronger precondition (NonEmptyArray<number> or readonly [number, ...number[]]). Push the constraint into the signature so callers cannot pass [] and the runtime guard collapses into the type.

issues.description: Empty-domain inputs now throw where previously they soft-failed to NaN/undefined
issues.detail: The prior implementation accepted any array; peek of empty returned undefined and arithmetic yielded NaN. The new implementation throws, strengthening the precondition of a published API. Any caller relying on the old soft-fail behavior breaks. Document the contract change in release notes and the type signature, or preserve non-throwing backward compatibility.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the non-emptiness guard fires
issues.detail: Math.sign(domain[0]) executes outside pan/zoom, so an empty domain passed to panLog yields Math.sign(undefined) = NaN before the guard ever runs. The precondition is asserted in the wrong place. Hoist the check to each public entry, or assert it before computing sign.

issues.description: Only panLinear/zoomLinear empty-domain throws are tested; six other entry points unproved
issues.detail: panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog share the same empty-domain precondition but no test exercises it. A one-line table-driven test over all eight entry points would prove the contract cheaply and document the new behavior, especially given the panLog/zoomLog sign-computation ordering issue.

issues.description: peek overload is correct but slightly more machinery than the data shape requires
issues.detail: Two overloads plus an implementation signature for array[length-1]. The non-empty branch is a sound ADT refinement, but if callers used NonEmptyArray at the boundary, peek would not need an overload at all. Document the precondition in JSDoc so callers reading types alone understand the contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR is a reasonable typing pass on working code, but two contract changes slipped in under the "types only" banner. First, coerceNumber silently maps null to 0 where the original propagated NaN — a quiet semantic shift flagged by all three reviewers. Second, empty domains now throw and the parameter type still says number[], so the contract is split between the type system and runtime guards instead of being expressed at the boundary as NonEmptyArray. Fix the signature, document the coercion choice, hoist the panLog/zoomLog sign computation behind the guard, and extend tests to all eight entry points before merge.
